task_summary: Implement a shared UI component library in TypeScript/React comprising CalloutBox, CodeBlock, VersionBadge, VideoEmbed, Sidebar, and PageLayout components, along with associated types (CalloutType enum, RouteEntry, RouteManifest, various Props interfaces). The library depends on 'app_routing' and must follow strict named-export conventions, composition-over-inheritance, and pass contract tests under vitest + @testing-library/react in jsdom.

findings.finding: PageLayout and Sidebar are classic composition containers. Best practice is to accept `children` as ReactNode and use slot-based props (e.g., `sidebar`, `header`, `content`) rather than deep prop-drilling. This aligns with the 'prefer composition over inheritance' mandate. PageLayout should compose Sidebar rather than extend it.
findings.relevance: Directly mandated by project standards. PageLayout wrapping Sidebar is a textbook composition scenario.

findings.topic: CodeBlock — Syntax Highlighting Without Third-Party Libraries
findings.finding: The project prefers stdlib over third-party libraries, which means avoiding prism.js, highlight.js, or shiki. A minimal CodeBlock can render a <pre><code> element with a `language` class (e.g., `language-typescript`) and defer actual syntax highlighting to CSS or a future integration. This keeps the component self-contained and testable without external deps. The CodeBlockLanguage type should constrain accepted language strings.
findings.source: HTML spec for <pre>/<code> semantics; project preference for stdlib
findings.relevance: Critical design decision — avoids bloating the shared library while leaving a clean extension point.

findings.finding: YouTube embeds should use youtube-nocookie.com domain for privacy, sandbox the iframe with `sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin'`, set `loading='lazy'`, and include `title` for accessibility. The YouTubeUrl type should validate or at least accept standard youtube.com/watch and youtu.be URL formats. XSS risk: never interpolate raw URL strings into src without validation — extract the video ID via regex and construct the embed URL deterministically.
findings.source: OWASP iframe embedding guidelines, YouTube IFrame API docs, web.dev performance best practices
findings.relevance: Security-critical: iframe src injection is a known XSS vector. Extracting video ID and rebuilding the URL is the safe pattern.

findings.finding: CalloutBox (info/warning/error/tip variants via CalloutType enum) should use `role='alert'` for error/warning types and `role='note'` or `role='status'` for info/tip. Use `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` for screen readers. Map CalloutType enum values to CSS class names and ARIA roles systematically. Common pitfall: forgetting to handle unknown enum values — always include a default/fallback case.
findings.source: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, MDN role documentation
findings.relevance: Accessibility is a baseline requirement for shared UI components; CalloutBox is the highest-risk component for ARIA misuse.

findings.finding: VersionBadge should accept a VersionString (likely semver-format) and render a styled badge. Edge cases: pre-release tags (e.g., '1.0.0-beta.1'), build metadata (e.g., '1.0.0+build.42'), and empty/undefined version strings. The component should gracefully handle invalid version strings rather than crashing. No need for a semver parsing library — a simple display component suffices unless comparison logic is required.
findings.source: semver.org specification, defensive UI component design patterns
findings.relevance: VersionString is a primitive type — validation should be lightweight; rendering should be resilient.

findings.topic: Sidebar + RouteManifest Integration with app_routing Dependency
findings.finding: Sidebar likely consumes RouteManifest (a list of RouteEntry structs) from the app_routing dependency to render navigation. CRITICAL per project rules: the string keys used in any map/registry (e.g., PageComponentKey enum values, route slugs) MUST be read from the app_routing module's exported types/enums/manifest — never inferred from component names. The contract test will verify exact key matching.
findings.source: Project operating procedures (String Keys in Maps and Registries rule)
findings.relevance: This is the highest-risk area for contract test failures. Must inspect app_routing exports before defining any key-based lookups.

findings.finding: Every .tsx file must: (1) `import React from 'react'` at the top, (2) export each component as both named and default (`export function Foo() {} ... export default Foo`), (3) export all types/interfaces/constants as named exports. Common pitfall: forgetting the default export on component files, or exporting types only via `export type` which may not satisfy certain test import patterns.
findings.relevance: Non-negotiable project rule. Every component file must follow this dual-export pattern.

findings.finding: vitest + @testing-library/react in jsdom cannot test: real CSS rendering, iframe loading, or layout. Tests should focus on: (1) correct DOM structure (role, class, data attributes), (2) prop-driven conditional rendering (e.g., CalloutType changes role/class), (3) content projection (children render in correct slots), (4) YouTube URL sanitization logic. Use `screen.getByRole`, `screen.getByText`, `screen.getByTestId` for assertions. Avoid snapshot tests for these components — they're brittle with frequent UI iteration.
findings.source: Testing Library best practices (testing-library.com/docs/guiding-principles), vitest jsdom documentation
findings.relevance: Contract tests must pass without external services; jsdom constraints shape what we can meaningfully verify.

findings.finding: With 6 components, associated types, and the 300-line-per-file limit, the recommended structure is: one file per component (.tsx), one shared types file (types.ts), and one barrel index.ts for re-exports. This keeps each file well under 300 lines. Avoid a monolithic components.tsx file.
findings.source: Project operating procedures (300-line limit), standard React project structure conventions
findings.relevance: Hard project constraint. With types + 6 components + tests, splitting is mandatory.

findings.finding: YouTube URLs come in many formats: youtube.com/watch?v=ID, youtu.be/ID, youtube.com/embed/ID, youtube-nocookie.com/embed/ID, with optional timestamps (?t=120), playlist params (?list=X), and shorts (youtube.com/shorts/ID). A robust extractor regex: /(?:youtube\.com\/(?:watch\?v=|embed\/|shorts\/)|youtu\.be\/)([a-zA-Z0-9_-]{11})/. Always extract the 11-char video ID and construct embed URL from it — never pass through raw URLs.
findings.source: YouTube URL format documentation, common open-source implementations (e.g., get-youtube-id npm package patterns)
findings.relevance: Directly impacts VideoEmbed correctness and security. Malformed URLs should result in no iframe rendered, not a broken/exploitable embed.

recommended_approach:
**File Structure:**
- `src/shared/types.ts` — All type definitions (CalloutType enum, CalloutBoxProps, CodeBlockLanguage, CodeBlockProps, VersionString, VersionBadgeProps, YouTubeUrl, VideoEmbedProps, RouteEntry, RouteManifest, SidebarProps, PageLayoutProps, PageComponentKey)
- `src/shared/CalloutBox.tsx` — CalloutBox component
- `src/shared/CodeBlock.tsx` — CodeBlock component  
- `src/shared/VersionBadge.tsx` — VersionBadge component
- `src/shared/VideoEmbed.tsx` — VideoEmbed with YouTube URL ID extraction + sanitized iframe
- `src/shared/Sidebar.tsx` — Sidebar consuming RouteManifest from app_routing
- `src/shared/PageLayout.tsx` — PageLayout composing Sidebar + content area
- `src/shared/index.ts` — Barrel re-exports
- `src/shared/__tests__/` — One test file per component

**Key Implementation Decisions:**
1. **VideoEmbed**: Extract 11-char YouTube video ID via regex, construct `https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/{ID}` deterministically. Return null/fallback for invalid URLs.
2. **CalloutBox**: Map CalloutType enum → ARIA role + CSS class. Use a `Record<CalloutType, {role: string, className: string}>` lookup.
3. **CodeBlock**: Render `<pre><code className={`language-${language}`}>` with text content. No runtime highlighting.
4. **Sidebar**: Accept RouteManifest (RouteEntry[]) as prop, render navigation links. Import route types from app_routing dependency — verify key strings against app_routing exports.
5. **PageLayout**: Accept sidebar content and main content via composition props. Render structural layout with semantic HTML (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<aside>`).
6. **PageComponentKey**: MUST be sourced from app_routing or contract test data — never inferred.

**Testing**: Each component gets render tests verifying DOM structure, ARIA attributes, conditional rendering per prop variants, and edge cases (empty props, invalid URLs).
alternatives_considered: Monolithic single-file approach: rejected due to 300-line limit and maintainability concerns.
Using third-party syntax highlighting (prism.js/highlight.js) for CodeBlock: rejected per stdlib preference; can be added later as opt-in enhancement.
Using third-party semver library for VersionBadge: rejected as unnecessary — component only displays, doesn't compare versions.
Render-prop pattern for PageLayout slots: considered but standard children + named slot props (sidebar, header) is simpler and more idiomatic for this use case.
CSS-in-JS (styled-components/emotion) for styling: rejected per stdlib preference; use CSS classes or inline styles.
risks: PageComponentKey enum values may not match between this component and app_routing — must verify against app_routing's exported types or contract test fixtures before implementation.
RouteManifest/RouteEntry structure assumed from type signature but actual shape depends on app_routing's exports — mismatch will cause type errors or runtime failures.
YouTube URL regex may miss edge-case formats (e.g., music.youtube.com, YouTube Shorts with query params) — should fail closed (render nothing) rather than open.
jsdom does not load iframes — VideoEmbed tests can only verify iframe element attributes, not actual embed behavior.
CalloutType enum values must exactly match contract expectations — if the contract test uses string literals like 'info' vs 'INFO', a case mismatch will fail.
The app_routing dependency may not yet be implemented — may need to define compatible interface types and import from the dependency's type definitions rather than runtime exports.
compliance_notes: All files must be .ts/.tsx — no Python generation under any circumstances.
Every component file must start with `import React from 'react'`.
Every component must have both named export and default export.
All public functions must have TypeScript type annotations.
All types, interfaces, constants must be named exports.
String keys in any map/registry must be verified against source of truth (app_routing exports or contract test data).
Use `import.meta.env.VITE_X` directly if any env vars are needed — never cast via `as any`.
Each file must stay under 300 lines.
Each function must have at least one test; tests must run without external services.
Prefer stdlib — no third-party UI libraries (no prism.js, no styled-components, etc.).
